newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs urge EU to forgive foreign debt.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs urge EU to forgive foreign debt.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday urged the EU member states to cancel the debt owed them by countries in Central and Latin America.
"The burden of debt is a significant factor in the desperate situation in these countries," parliament said in a report on relations between the European Union and the countries of Central America.
The report by Spanish United Left MEP Carlos Carnero Gonzales comes in response to a communication from the European Commission, COM(95)600, on ways of improving the so-called San Jose dialogue.
Since 1984 the San Jose dialogue has provided for annual talks between the foreign ministers of the EU and Costa Rica, El Salvador Honduras, Guatemala, Nicaragua and Panama.
Parliament agreed it was important to intensify these contacts, the main aim of which is to establish permanent peace and democracy in Central America, and improve social and economic conditions.

In a separate report on prospects for strengthening ties between the EU and the Latin America states, parliament reiterated a request the EU to forgive part of each country's debt and bring in new debt-for-nature/education swaps.

Drafted by Dutch Liberal Jan-Willem Bertens, this second report criticises as unambitious the Commission's proposals for strengthening EU relations with Latin America over the next three years, COM(95)495.

Parliament warned that if the EU did not step up investment in Latin America's emerging economies and its political influence with the region's leaders, then it risked being outflanked by the United States.
Euro-MPs suggested the EU establish a trans-Atlantic dialogue with Latin America along the lines of the fora it has set up for talks with the U.S. and Canada.
